whatItIs.text: A sour citrus whose juice runs about 5-6% citric acid — the backbone of lemonade, dressings, and the finishing squeeze on almost everything.

historyNote.text: The lemon is a hybrid of citron and bitter orange, probably born in northeastern India in the first millennium BC; it reached Europe by the second century AD and spread through the Arab Agricultural Revolution between 1000 and 1150.

howToChoose.text: Choose lemons that feel heavy for their size with fine, oily skin — weight means juice; hard or dull-skinned ones are often dry inside.

storage.text: Refrigerate in the crisper for weeks, or juice and freeze in cubes.

foodSafetyRef.note: Practice storage guidance only; no rulebook content is claimed. The app's food-safety rules live in data/food-safety/rules.json.

useItUp.text: A tired lemon still has zest and juice: grate the zest first, squeeze the rest into ice-cube trays, and drop spent halves into the compost bin or the kettle to descale.

substitutions.note: in dressings and marinades; no citrus aroma
